liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dire Wolf** (1 review): Opening Dire Wolf brought a smile and a tear to this listener [8]

## Setlist highlights

- **keep the aisles clear**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-10-22.nak300.morris.101778.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 28 songs; 166 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: Tape was flipped between drums and space, and some crowd noise and tuning were removed [1]
- **gd1980-10-22.sonyecm280.wise.miller.100416.flac16**: source not stated; 27 songs; 171 min [2]
- **gd80-10-22.sony.wiley.8479.sbefail.shnf**: audience recording; 26 songs; 168 min; rated 3.9/5 by 10 [4]. Said about its sound: Low-generation audience tape that is crisp, but the tapers shift their microphones about once per song, making it hard listening; Recording sounds like the closest taper's pair of microphones aimed out toward the audience; Audience tape has a noisy fan that can intrude during jam peaks [6][10][15]
- **gd1980-10-22.120053.fob-nak700.gatto-jaeger.dusborne.flac16**: source not stated; 27 songs; 169 min [3]

## Around the show

- The Radio City setting impressed the writer, and slides from the band's career were projected during the show [6]
- Attended at age 15, about four shows in; called it the first acoustic sets since the sixties [7]
- Reviewer sat in the first balcony row, clapping and cheering, beside several tapers, with the mixing board right behind [10]
- Both the acoustic and electric sets are enjoyed; the recording is audience-sourced and of modest quality [11]
- Taper's friends kept advising him to pause the recorder until Jerry returned, which proved bad advice [12]
- Taping at Radio City in 1980 was difficult, so any tape from the venue is valuable [15]
- As the first night at Radio City, security was strict on tapers, and several were caught [16]
- Writer considers these Radio City shows underrated and overlooked [6]
- Reviewer ranks it as the weaker show of the New York run and of the whole fall tour [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-10-22.nak300.morris.101778.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Bob Morris; transferred by Bob Morris; source: Nakamichi CM-300 (CP-1) x2 > Cassette Master (Marantz Superscope CD320/Maxell UDXLII-C90) [1]. Also: This is the only audience-only recording among the 18 shows of the fall 1980 three-set run [16]
- **gd1980-10-22.sonyecm280.wise.miller.100416.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Sony ECM-280 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXLII-C90/Dolby B) [2]. Also: Transferred from Jim Wise's master cassettes, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones [2]
- **gd80-10-22.sony.wiley.8479.sbefail.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-280 mics [4]
- **gd1980-10-22.120053.fob-nak700.gatto-jaeger.dusborne.flac16**: taped by Keith Gatto & Pete Jaeger; transferred by Michael Turi; source: Lodge Dead front center; Nak 700 > sony D-5> AMC> DAT> CDR> EAC> TLH> Flac; Recorded by Keith Gatto & Pete Jaeger; Extracted & flac encoded by Michael Turi;… [3]
